Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Local co-op profiles

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Browser play uses the shared asynchronous IndexedDB store. The game waits for its identity and profile before opening the Replay runtime, which schedules simulation steps and retains input/history. Identity creation uses a create-only transaction; a competing creator's identity is loaded instead of overwritten. Profile writes compare the last loaded revision and only mark progress saved after a transaction completion receipt. A competing write stops local saving and reports unsaved progress. It never replaces newer storage automatically. The HUD distinguishes saving from saved loadout/upgrades.

The default browser database is replay/scrapyard, scoped to the page's origin. profile_namespace selects a separate database for fixtures. As on native, explicit token values disable persistence unless persist=1 is supplied. The browser uses the same validated profile codec and cooperative owner-claim policy described below. It does not import a native profile. Runs and spray preferences use separate save operations; an upgrade receipt does not save the current run. Browser eviction/deletion can remove local progress; portable power-loss durability is not claimed.

web_profile_run.sh earns two floor-clear cores, buys a plate, kills Chrome and starts a new browser with the same isolated disk profile. It checks the unchanged identity/profile bytes, restored choices and 14-HP plate entry. It also preserves the competing record after a revision conflict, and refuses a corrupted profile before a session opens. Original Scrapyard data remains separate.

Native interactive play keeps a stable random reconnect identity in this project's user://replay_identity and a separate canonical profile record keyed by its token hash. The Godot project uses the replay_scrapyard user-data directory; no original Scrapyard profile is imported, overwritten or cleared. Explicit fixture tokens disable persistence by default. Tests can opt in with RSY_PERSIST=1 and an isolated RSY_PROFILE_DIR. Two local player processes need different identities: use different existing profile directories, or an explicit fixture token for a temporary second player. Reusing one identity concurrently is deliberately rejected.

The version-2 record stores automatic/explicit choice modes, the identity binding, cores/parts, accepted staging preferences, and the epoch/tick of the last saved change. Version-1 records remain readable as explicit choices. Checksums, schema/version and value validation reject malformed records. Identity mismatch rejects a record copied to another account path. A malformed existing identity/profile fails opening instead of silently creating a replacement identity or resetting progress.

This preserves the original cooperative owner-claim trust model. The host accepts an opening meta claim once per occupant. Later lobby declarations cannot restore spent cores or replace earned state; reconnect/migration keeps the existing claimed state. This local file is editable by its owner and is not a competitive economy service or an anti-cheat mechanism.

Only authority observations are saved—never speculative purchases or predicted rewards. The owner writes a staged file, flushes/closes it, then renames it over the previous record. The previous file and in-memory saved record remain unchanged if writing fails; the game reports that failure visibly. This is a process-crash boundary, not a portable power-loss/fsync guarantee. After recovery, the installed authority state wins over an older local claim; possible checkpoint rollback remains part of the room's declared recovery policy.

Lobby settings are idempotent declarations. Stale/future rejections of the latest local declaration or Ready setter trigger a new declaration; updates preserve the owner's desired readiness. Other players' action sequences do not trigger retries. Casts and purchases keep their explicit action outcomes rather than being blindly reissued as new transactions.

profile_run.sh earns cores through two real floors, buys a plate, closes Godot and opens a fresh process with the same identity. It verifies the restored part, health and loadout, then checks both corruption rejection and preservation of the old file when a staged write cannot open. Its files live in a temporary directory.
